title: Completed local ring of A[x] is formally smooth over A for its adic topology
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $A[x]$ the polynomial ring in one variable [def-weil-polynomial-ring], $\mathfrak q\subset A[x]$ a prime ideal, $T=A[x]_{\mathfrak q}$ the localization at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qT$, and $C=T^\wedge=\varprojlim_nT/\mathfrak q^nT$ its $\mathfrak qT$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], an $A$-algebra via $A\to A[x]\to T\to C$. Then $C$ is formally smooth over $A$ for the $\mathfrak qC$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic].

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07PU (lemma-another-helper-G-ring, line 12494), sentence 'As A -> A[x]_q^ is formally smooth (see Lemmas 07EC and 07ED)'; Lemma Tag 07EC (lemma-formally-smooth, line 9165) part (1), Lemma Tag 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion, line 9224) (1) => (2); A -> A[x] formally smooth (polynomial algebra) and A[x] -> A[x]_q formally smooth (localization) in the sense of Algebra, Definition 00TI

proof.text: *$A\to A[x]$ has the square-zero lifting property.* By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth] (with $C=A$, $n=1$, $y_1=x$) the ring map $A\to A[x]$ is smooth, so by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-square-zero-lifting] for every $A$-algebra $D$, every ideal $N\subseteq D$ with $N^2=0$, $q:D\to D/N$ the quotient map, and every $A$-algebra map $g_0:A[x]\to D/N$ there is an $A$-algebra map $f_0:A[x]\to D$ with $q\circ f_0=g_0$. (This is Algebra, Lemma 00TK; directly: send $x$ to any preimage of $g_0(x)$ under the surjection $q$.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00TK (lemma-polynomial-ring-formally-smooth, line 37849) and Proposition Tag 00TN (proposition-smooth-formally-smooth)

proof.text: *$A\to T$ has the square-zero lifting property.* $T=A[x]_{\mathfrak q}$ is the localization of $A[x]$ at $W=A[x]\setminus\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; let $\lambda:A[x]\to T$ be the canonical map. Let $D$ be an $A$-algebra, $N\subseteq D$ with $N^2=0$, $q:D\to D/N$, and $g:T\to D/N$ an $A$-algebra map. By step 1 applied to $g_0=g\circ\lambda$ there is an $A$-algebra map $f_0:A[x]\to D$ with $q\circ f_0=g\circ\lambda$. Regard $D$ as an $A[x]$-algebra via $f_0$; then $D/N$ is an $A[x]$-algebra via $q\circ f_0=g\circ\lambda$, so $g$ is a homomorphism of $A[x]$-algebras $T\to D/N$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-square-zero-lifting] (with $R=A[x]$, $W$, $R'=T$) there is an $A[x]$-algebra map $f:T\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$. Since $f\circ\lambda=f_0$ and $f_0$ is an $A$-algebra map, and the $A$-algebra structure of $T$ is $A\to A[x]\xrightarrow{\lambda}T$, $f$ is a homomorphism of $A$-algebras. (This is the composition argument of Algebra, Lemma 031H, whose proof Stacks omits.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 04EG (lemma-localization-formally-etale, line 41241) and Lemma Tag 031H (lemma-compose-formally-smooth, line 37839, proof omitted, written out here)

proof.text: *$T$ is formally smooth over $A$ for the $\mathfrak qT$-adic topology.* By [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] (with $R=A$, $S=T$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak qT$) one must lift every $A$-algebra map $g:T\to D/N$ with $g((\mathfrak qT)^k)=0$ for some $k\ge1$ to an $A$-algebra map $f:T\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$; step 2 gives such an $f$ for every $g$, without the condition on $(\mathfrak qT)^k$. This is Lemma 07EC (1) (formally smooth in the sense of Algebra 00TI implies formally smooth for any adic topology) for the definition of the DAG, where it is an instance of the definition.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07EC (lemma-formally-smooth, line 9165), part (1)

proof.text: *$\mathfrak qT$ is finitely generated.* $A[x]$ is a finite type $A$-algebra ($A[x_1]/(0)$), so it is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]; its localization $T$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]; hence every ideal of $T$, in particular $\mathfrak qT$, is finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion, line 9224): its hypothesis that the ideals are finitely generated

proof.text: *Passage to the completion.* By step 4 and step 3, [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-completion] applies with $R=A$, $S=T$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak qT$: $S^\wedge=\varprojlim_nT/\mathfrak q^nT=C$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], with $A$-algebra structure $A\to A[x]\to T\to C$, is formally smooth over $A$ for the $(\mathfrak qT)C$-adic topology. The ideal $(\mathfrak qT)C$ of $C$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak qT$ equals the ideal $\mathfrak qC$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak q$ (every element of $\mathfrak qT$ is $\lambda(a)\lambda(s)^{-1}$ with $a\in\mathfrak q$, and $\lambda(s)^{-1}$ maps into $C$), which is the claim.
